Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatease (FBPase) deﬁciency
FBPase deﬁciency is an autosomal recessive disease, caused by a genetic defect of FBPase (Tran, 2017). FBPase has a critical role in
the enzyme complex regulating glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. FBPase deﬁciency inhibits glucose production from lactate, glycerol
and gluconeogenic amino acids. It is diagnosed in infants within the ﬁrst weeks of life, when they become dependent on carbohy-
drate metabolism. When infants are fasting, normoglycemia is maintained by glycogenolysis and depends on the availability of
